_meta.verses: 19:42, 6:76, 21:69 complete, edition eng-ummmuhammad (fawazahmed0 quran-api); name Ibrahim

s1a: Shhh… Noah, Ilyas, are you still awake? Good! Tonight I will tell you the story of a young man who stood alone against a whole city, and of a great fire that could not harm him.
s1b: A fire that doesn't burn? Grandma, that's impossible!
s1c: Oh yes, my dear. When Allah wants something, it happens. Snuggle in… tonight I will tell you about the Prophet Ibrahim, peace be upon him.
s2a: A very long time ago, Ibrahim lived in a city full of statues. People made them with their own hands from stone and wood, and then they worshipped them. They bowed to them, put food in front of them and asked them for help.
s2b: Even Azar, Ibrahim's father, did that. But Ibrahim looked closely at the statues and thought: they cannot hear, they cannot see, they cannot even move.
s2c: Allah says in the Qur'an: "[Mention] when he said to his father, 'O my father, why do you worship that which does not hear and does not see and will not benefit you at all?'"
s2d: And what did his father say?
s2e: He became very angry. But Ibrahim stayed kind to him, and only said: Peace be upon you, my father.
s3a: Allah says: "So when the night covered him [with darkness], he saw a star. He said, 'This is my lord.' But when it set, he said, 'I like not those that disappear.'"
s3b: Then the moon rose, big and silver. He said: This is my lord. But the moon set too.
s3c: In the morning the sun rose, huge and shining. He said: This is my lord, this is bigger. But in the evening, the sun set as well.
s3d: Then Ibrahim called out: O my people, I have nothing to do with what you worship. I turn to the One who created the heavens and the earth.
s3e: Grandma, didn't Ibrahim know that before?
s3f: Clever question! Yes, he knew. He wanted to show his people something important: everything that disappears cannot be a god. Only Allah remains forever.
s4a: And Ibrahim had a brave plan. When the people had left the city, he went into the temple very quietly.
s4b: There stood the statues with food in front of them. Ibrahim asked them: Why don't you eat? Why don't you speak? And then… crash! He broke them all.
s4c: All except the biggest statue. When the people came back, they cried: Who did this to our gods?
s4d: Some of them said: We heard a young man speak badly of them. His name is Ibrahim.
s4e: They asked him: Did you do this, Ibrahim? And Ibrahim said: No, the biggest of them did it. So ask them, if they can speak.
s4f: Everyone went quiet, because they all knew these statues cannot speak.
s4h: Yes, my dear. Ibrahim wanted them to think for themselves and understand: a statue can do nothing, it cannot even help itself.
s5a: But instead of thinking, they became even angrier. They shouted: Burn him! So they built a big building for him and lit a huge, hot fire in it.
s5b: Then they threw Ibrahim into it. What do you think? Was Ibrahim afraid? Ibrahim only said: Hasbiyallahu wa ni'mal wakil. That means: Allah is enough for me, and He is the best one to trust.
s5c: Allah says: "Allah said, 'O fire, be coolness and safety upon Ibrahim.'" And the fire obeyed. It became cool and did not harm Ibrahim at all.
s5e: Yes! Everything obeys Allah: the wind, the water, and even the fire.
s6a: The people wanted to harm Ibrahim, but Allah made their plan fail. And Allah saved Ibrahim and Lut, who believed in him, and brought them to a blessed land.
s6b: And Allah took Ibrahim as a close friend. That is why we call him Khalilullah, the friend of Allah.
s6c: Oh… they are asleep. My dears, whoever trusts in Allah, Allah is enough for him, even if everyone else does wrong. Be brave like Ibrahim and stay with the truth, but always kindly, just as he was with his father. And if you are ever afraid, say: Hasbiyallahu wa ni'mal wakil.
s6d: And next time I will tell you about Lut, and about a city that did not want to listen to him.
s6e: And you, watching us right now: if you liked the story, ask your parents to subscribe to our channel, so you don't miss the next story. Good night, my dears. May Allah protect you.
